title: project
description: project.json at the tree root: aliases (@name -> a path under the root), plugins and their settings, secrets (key -> environment variable), and profiles choosing a binding per domain port. A port with exactly one binding in the tree needs no profile entry.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/project.schema.json.

description.description: What this tree is for, in one or two sentences, shown wherever a reader meets the project.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

aliases.description: Alias roots this tree may name, each mapping an @name to a folder path from the root. An alias may not collide with a plugin root or a reserved root (D007).

additionalProperties.description: A folder path from the root, e.g. @features/tasks.

plugins.description: The plugins this tree uses, each named by the alias root it takes and the package that ships it. Everything effectful enters through one of these.

from.description: The npm package that ships this plugin, imported by the runtime from the project's node_modules. Absent for the plugins built into the runtime (@std, @cli). A package name, never a file path.

settings.description: The values the plugin's settings contract judges. May read {{secrets.key}} and nothing else.

includes.description: Trees this one includes, by npm package name, never a path: each package's features/ loads as if it sat in this tree -- the same paths, the same rules, bound by bindings and profiles, visible through exports and dependsOn. `features` picks which of its features come along (default: all). The include's aliases come along (D007 on a collision); its connections, plugins, settings, startup and profiles do not: configuring a tree is the host's job, and a port the include leaves unbound is the host's to bind (B002 says which). A feature both local and included is refused (D009); a package that is not a wilanis tree, or one using a plugin this project does not name, is D010.

from.description: The npm package that ships the tree, installed in this project's package.json.

features.description: The features to include, by name; absent: every feature the package ships.

description.description: Why this tree is included, for a reader deciding whether it is still wanted.

blobs.description: The blob registry: where uploaded and generated files are kept while a run uses them. Files never pass through the engine; a graph holds a handle and the registry holds the bytes.

dir.description: The directory the registry writes to, relative to the project root or absolute. Absent: a directory under the system temp dir.

connection.description: The connection the registry keeps bytes behind, whose kind a plugin the project names offers a blob store for (C014): an object store, so a tree runs on many instances. Absent: files, under dir.

startup.description: What runs once when the tree is served, in this order, after every plugin's postLoad and before any trigger kind starts. Each entry names a domain port operation; the active profile's binding decides how it is met, so a connection can be real in one profile and a fake in another. This is where a pool is opened, a queue declared, a topic subscribed: the work is declared here rather than hidden in a plugin's code, so a reader sees at the root what happens before the first request. An entry takes no request -- nothing has been received yet -- so the operation it names must not read request.*. wilanis serve runs these; wilanis check, rehearse and run do not.

description.description: What this step starts, for a reader of wilanis start.

label.description: A short human name for this step, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of the operation path.

run.description: The domain port operation this step fires, as path#operation. Never a graph: the step says what it wants done, and the port's binding decides how.

in.description: Every value the operation takes, written as literals. A startup step runs before anything is received, so only const and {{secrets.*}} may appear here -- never {{request.*}}.

required.description: Whether serving may proceed when this step refuses. true (the default): serve stops and exits nonzero, so a tree whose database is unreachable never opens its port. false: the refusal is logged, the remaining steps run, and the trigger kinds start anyway.

profiles.description: The profiles this step runs under, by name; absent: every profile. Every name is one project.json declares (B012). The startup list stays one list in one order, so a reader sees at the root what every place starts.

secrets.description: The secrets this tree reads, each mapping a name a setting may reference to the environment variable that holds it (C001).

additionalProperties.description: The environment variable that holds the secret: UPPER_CASE.

profiles.description: The places a tree runs, so one tree can be met differently in each: which binding meets each domain port, which connection stands in for another, and which profile a start runs under when none is named.

description.description: What this profile is for, so a reader knows when to run under it.

default.description: The profile a start runs under when neither --profile nor WILANIS_PROFILE names one. At most one profile is the default (C017).

connections.description: Which connection stands in for another under this profile: every reference to the left-hand connection reaches the right-hand one, a different connection document of the same kind, or, for a broker, of another kind declaring the same delivery (C018). The mapping is one step: a stand-in that is itself a key is not followed.

propertyNames.description: A connection path (@...) the documents name, replaced under this profile by the connection it maps to.

bindings.description: Which binding meets each domain port under this profile. Every domain port needs exactly one (B002).

propertyNames.description: A domain port path (@...), bound to the binding document that meets it under this profile.
